import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import pearsonr

# Load the data from the CSV file
df = pd.read_csv('table_name.csv')

# Select the relevant columns by name for clarity
composite_score = df['Indices of Deprivation 2015 - South East U.A.s (n.b. Rank 1 = most deprived).1']
percentage_affected = df['Indices of Deprivation 2015 - South East U.A.s (n.b. Rank 1 = most deprived).3']

# Check for missing values and handle them if necessary
if composite_score.isnull().any() or percentage_affected.isnull().any():
    print("Warning: Missing values detected. Consider handling them before analysis.")

# Perform Pearson correlation test
corr, p_value = pearsonr(composite_score, percentage_affected)

# Output the results
print("Correlation Method: Pearson")
print(f"Correlation Coefficient: {corr}")
print(f"P-value: {p_value}")
